entries.clue: Quarrel spanning hundred and ten years expelling leader who's out of touch? (5,5)

annotation.definitionNote: reads as 'one who's out of touch'; the answer is a noun for such a person

indicators.note: the quarrel stretches across the next pieces, holding them inside
the ten years lose their first letter

blocks.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
C is the Roman numeral for 100
DECADE without its first letter D

annotation.surface: A long-running row between two people drifting so far apart that one has lost all touch.
annotation.walkthrough: Space cadet is an informal term for a dreamy person out of touch with reality; the question mark flags the loose definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A space cadet is a person who seems to live in a world of their own.

entries.clue: Break hands on the blower (5)

indicators.note: the blower is British slang for the telephone, so we hear the word rather than see it

blocks.note: paws are hands, informally

annotation.surface: Someone taking a break by getting their hands on the phone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The blower' is British slang for the telephone, which is how the clue signals that the word is heard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pause and a break are both a brief stop.

entries.clue: Wire securing pedal in furniture (6,5)

indicators.note: the wire holds the next piece fast inside it

blocks.note: a cable is a wire
pedal means 'of feet', written as OF FEET

annotation.surface: A trailing wire tangled round a pedal in a room full of furniture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pedal' is the adjective meaning relating to the feet, as in pedal extremities, so it gives a phrase rather than anything on a bike.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this low table is one kind of furniture.

entries.clue: Desperately target ice burn (9)

indicators.note: done desperately, the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A frantic attempt to aim at ice and cause a burn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Burn' is British slang for a cigarette or tobacco, which hides well behind its sense of an injury.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang a burn is a smoke, a cigarette.

entries.clue: Get off updated version of Tinder adult breaks (7)

indicators.note: a new version rearranges the letters
the A breaks into the rearranged word

blocks.note: TINDER rearranged
A is the film rating for adult

annotation.surface: Someone quitting a dating app whose new version lets adults barge in.
annotation.walkthrough: The dating app is a red herring: Tinder supplies only six letters of fodder, with the adult breaking into them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly railway language: to leave a train.

entries.clue: Shy host (5)

blocks.note: shy as a verb: to fling, as at a coconut shy
host as a verb: to put on a party

annotation.walkthrough: Both words are verbs here: 'shy' is not timid but to fling, and 'host' is what you do when you throw a party.
annotation.definitionFit: Shy is the old verb to fling, as at a fairground coconut shy, and you host a party by throwing one.

entries.clue: Take part in school sports sick (4)

blocks.note: to do something is to take part in it
PE is physical education, school sports

annotation.surface: A pupil who feels ill but still has to join in games lessons.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sick' is not ill here: in slang both sick and dope mean excellent.
annotation.definitionFit: In slang, sick and dope both mean brilliant.

entries.clue: Left bill over dish (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means read from the bottom up

blocks.note: L is left
an ad, a bill posted up

annotation.surface: Someone leaving the bill on top of their dish at a restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill' means a poster here, not a restaurant bill, despite the dish.
annotation.definitionFit: Dal is an Indian dish of spiced lentils.

entries.clue: Potentially feature mistakes of learner overwhelmed by street hazards (4,5)

indicators.note: the learner is swamped, sitting inside the hazards

blocks.note: L is the learner-driver plate
potholes are hazards in the road

annotation.surface: A learner driver swamped by the potholes on their street.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feature' means a feature film, and 'potentially' allows that other stories have them too.
annotation.definitionFit: Plot holes are gaps in a story's logic, a feature film's typical mistakes.

entries.clue: Where Spooner's entertaining with something to eat? (8)

annotation.definition: Where Spooner's entertaining with something to eat?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: something entertaining is fun; it gives up its F and takes the B
a bite is something to eat; it hands over its B and takes the F

annotation.surface: A question about the sort of place where guests are entertained with food.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a bunfight is a tea party, where people are entertained with something to eat.
annotation.definitionFit: A bunfight is British slang for a tea party or other gathering with food.

entries.clue: Soon let's hope for solution to BO (4-2)

blocks.note: an idiom urging a future event, like the weekend, to hurry up
BO is body odour; the solution is a deodorant applied with a rolling ball

annotation.walkthrough: BO is body odour; 'solution' is both the answer to a problem and a liquid, which is what a roll-on holds.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Roll on' wishes something would come soon, and a roll-on deodorant cures BO.

entries.clue: Shared bit of content egotist's mantra? (4)

blocks.note: an image or joke that spreads online
what a self-obsessed person repeats: the word for oneself, twice

annotation.walkthrough: The second half is playful: split the answer as ME ME and it is what a self-obsessed person chants.
annotation.definitionFit: A meme is an image or joke shared widely online.

entries.clue: Fine for driving Tory Howard when drunk (10)

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A Conservative politician who is fine to drive only once he has had a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that drunk is exactly when you are not fit to drive; Michael Howard led the Conservatives in 2003 to 2005.
annotation.definitionFit: A roadworthy vehicle is fit to be driven.

entries.clue: According to instruction, knits article or object? (5,1,5)

indicators.note: the answer is itself an instruction: RAISE (reverse, in a down entry) A STINK

blocks.note: the instruction word, telling you to lift the rest upward
KNITS plus A (article), which reads upward as A STINK

annotation.surface: Someone knitting to a pattern and asking whether an item is a thing or an object.
annotation.walkthrough: This works backwards: obey the answer, raising A STINK in a down entry, and you get KNITS A, which is what the clue shows. 'Object' is the verb, to protest.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: making a loud fuss is a way to object, the verb meaning to protest.

entries.clue: Bird following two big signs hit the roof (4,2)

indicators.note: the bird comes after the signs

blocks.note: L (large) and OS (outsize), two clothing labels meaning big
a tit is a small bird

annotation.surface: A bird trailing two large signs flies up and hits a roof.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'big signs' are size labels on clothes: L for large and OS for outsize.
annotation.definitionFit: To lose it and to hit the roof both mean to lose your temper.

entries.clue: Now likely later to become ill (2,3,4)

blocks.note: as in 'the match is on', going ahead
then = afterwards
to ail is to fall sick

annotation.surface: A warning that something is fine now but is likely to go wrong later.
annotation.walkthrough: Paying on the nail means paying immediately, so the answer means now.
annotation.definitionFit: On the nail means at once, as in payment made on the nail.

entries.clue: Casually plan suit without head of union (7)

indicators.note: done casually, the letters are loosely thrown together
the suit loses its first letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder
SUIT without its head, S

annotation.surface: Someone casually drawing up a design for a suit, but leaving off the union's leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of union' wants to be U, but 'head' belongs to the suit and 'of union' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to marriage, the union of two people.

entries.clue: Teen's crushing score of zero after pressure at university exhausted possibly (5,4)

indicators.note: the zero comes after the rest
the word is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

blocks.note: P is pressure in physics
up = in residence at university
POSSIBLY emptied, leaving its first and last letters
love is a zero score in tennis

annotation.surface: A teenager crushed by a zero result after being put under pressure at university.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crushing' is the noun sense of having a crush, not squashing. 'Exhausted' means emptied here, not tired.
annotation.definitionFit: Puppy love is a teenager's short-lived crush.

entries.clue: Picture representing key field essential to agriculture (7)

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre

blocks.note: Tab is a key on a keyboard
a lea is a meadow
the middle letter of the 11-letter AGRICULTURE

annotation.surface: A painting of a field, an essential feature of farming.
annotation.walkthrough: Lea is an old poetic word for a meadow, common in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picture or a scene arranged like one.

entries.clue: Having plans for Nirvana, Kurt regularly moving over to front of instrument (7)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of the name, starting with the second
the last letter, O, is moved to the front of the word

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of KURT
PIANO with its O shifted to the front

annotation.surface: Kurt Cobain of Nirvana switching to a piano for the band's new songs.
annotation.walkthrough: Nirvana is the band fronted by Kurt Cobain, but here it means a perfect state; Utopian plans aim at one.
annotation.definitionFit: Utopian describes plans for an ideal, perfect world.

entries.clue: Give me a break quietly when shelter checks (6)

indicators.note: the shelter holds the next word in check, inside it

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music
the lee is the sheltered side
as = when

annotation.surface: A plea for rest, quietly made while the shelter is inspected.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Please!' said with scorn means 'give me a break', I don't believe you.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Please!' and 'give me a break!' are both exasperated retorts.

entries.clue: European politician fills in words of Conservative expecting obedience (10)

indicators.note: the European politician fills a gap inside the next phrase

blocks.note: per Tory = according to a Conservative
E for European
an MP is a Member of Parliament

annotation.surface: A European politician speaking for a Conservative who demands to be obeyed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'European politician' tempts as an MEP, but it splits as European plus Member of Parliament. 'In words of' means according to, as in 'per the manual'.
annotation.definitionFit: A peremptory tone insists on immediate obedience.

entries.clue: Fruit from food for baby that I find adorable (5)

blocks.note: pap is soft food for babies
'aw!' is what you say at something cute

annotation.surface: Fruit mashed from baby food, which the speaker finds adorable.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation AW stands for the whole phrase 'that I find adorable'.
annotation.definitionFit: Papaw is another name for the papaya, or a North American fruit.

entries.clue: Average broadcasts for audience (2-2)

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads

blocks.note: to sow is to broadcast seed; two broadcasts are two sows

annotation.surface: Middling ratings for broadcasts that play to an audience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasts' is farming, not radio: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering.
annotation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre, just average.

entries.clue: I sent ugly mug (5)

indicators.note: the letters are made ugly, twisted out of shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters

annotation.surface: Someone who sent out an unflattering face, an ugly mug.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ugly mug' is a stock phrase for an unattractive face, but 'mug' is the drinking vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a German-style beer mug.

entries.clue: Accept better offer than that of leader with university course change withdrawn (6)

annotation.definition: Accept better offer than that of

indicators.note: drawn back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the Prime Minister leads the government
U for university
a zag is a sharp change of course

annotation.surface: A leader pulling a student's request to switch course after accepting a better offer.
annotation.walkthrough: In British house sales, a seller gazumps a buyer by taking a higher offer after agreeing to theirs.
annotation.definitionFit: To gazump a buyer is to accept a higher offer than theirs after agreeing a sale.

entries.clue: Beauford stocks rarely-seen transport (3)

indicators.note: the name holds the answer in stock inside it

blocks.note: beaUFOrd

annotation.surface: A car dealer called Beauford keeping an unusual vehicle in stock.
annotation.walkthrough: A UFO, a flying saucer, is transport that is very rarely seen.
annotation.definitionFit: A UFO is a craft seldom sighted.

entries.clue: Glorified marriage commitment created falsehood to protect son (8)

indicators.note: the falsehood wraps round the son to shield him

blocks.note: 'I do' is said at the wedding
to lie is to make up a falsehood
S for son

annotation.surface: A glorified wedding vow turned out to be a lie told to shield a son.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Created falsehood' is one verb phrase: to make up a falsehood is to lie, here in the past tense.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone glorified is worshipped like an idol.

entries.clue: Variety show that's disappointing group of stars reportedly (4)

indicators.note: what we are told, so heard not seen

blocks.note: 'oh!' is a disappointed sigh, and Leo is a constellation

annotation.surface: A variety show with a disappointing line-up of stars, by all accounts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Group of stars' reads as a celebrity cast but is a constellation.
annotation.definitionFit: An olio is a miscellany, including a variety entertainment.

entries.clue: Prodigy's flaw ultimately: not good enough! (10)

indicators.note: in the end, so the word's final letter

blocks.note: the last letter of FLAW
read as 'under-kind': UNDER (short of the mark) plus KIND (good)

annotation.surface: A child prodigy's fatal weakness: never quite good enough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prodigy's' is prodigy is: the apostrophe s joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A loanword: German for 'wonder child', used in English for a young prodigy.
